# Fundamental Analysis: 4062.T

## 1. Executive conclusion

- **Fundamental rating: Neutral.** The business is excellent and the demand backdrop is unusually visible; the stock is not cheap enough, and the near-term forecast offers no edge over guidance or consensus.
- **Decision horizon:** 3–6 months (to ~end-April 2027).
- **Business direction:** Strongly positive. Advanced IC package substrates are supply-constrained, and management expects the shortfall to persist to CY2030 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
- **Earnings direction:** Strongly positive. H1 FY3/27 operating profit rose 84.6% YoY to ¥60.1bn on revenue of ¥262.5bn (+34.3%) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1].
- **Forecast versus guidance:** FY3/27 model equals guidance ([[565.0]] revenue, [[133.0]] OP, [[89.0]] net) because it is built as H1 actual plus the disclosed H2 guidance split — no edge. FY3/28 model OP of [[190.0]] is 15% above management's ¥165bn, on reversal of the ~¥10bn price-decline buffer plus Cell 8/mix upside.
- **Forecast versus consensus:** FY3/28 OP model [[190.0]] equals the consensus figure cited by Citi — **no material forecast edge**.
- **Cash-flow quality:** Weak on a normalized basis. H1 operating cash flow of ¥193.2bn was inflated by a ¥118.8bn increase in customer advances; excluding that, underlying operating cash flow was ~¥74bn against ¥48.9bn of capex [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9–10].
- **Balance-sheet condition:** Strong. Net cash of ~¥258bn (cash ¥420.5bn vs interest-bearing debt ¥162.0bn), equity ratio 53.5% [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1, p.4–5].
- **Valuation:** Demanding. At [[8,045]] the stock is 51.2x FY3/27 EPS of [[157.2]] and ~37–39x FY3/28 EPS of [[215.4]] (39x on a fully diluted ~595m share count), with negative normalized free cash flow. My fair-value range is ¥7,000–8,400, i.e. roughly flat to −13% from spot.
- **Main catalyst (within horizon):** Decision and disclosure on Cell 7 / Cell 9 investment, and a possible revision of the FY3/30 (¥1,000bn revenue / ¥300bn OP) target, both guided to occur by end-FY3/27 [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].
- **Main risk:** A third AI-GPU substrate supplier plus a capital programme that consumes cash; the scarcity premium can compress before reported earnings are affected [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].
- **Principal limitation:** No revenue, net-profit or EPS consensus is available; only an FY3/28 operating-profit consensus figure exists. Two internal notes carry unverified publication timestamps.

*Fiscal-year note:* the company labels the year ending March 2027 "FY2026". This report uses FY3/27 for that year, FY3/28 for the year ending March 2028, and so on.

---

## 2. Company and earnings structure

4062.T (Ibiden Co., Ltd.) makes money in three reported segments, of which one dominates:

| H1 FY3/27 segment | Revenue (¥m) | Segment profit (¥m) | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Electronics (IC package substrates) | 172,540 | 50,028 | 29.0% |
| Ceramics (DPF, EV, graphite) | 46,156 | 5,391 | 11.7% |
| Others | 43,849 | 4,623 | 10.5% |
| Consolidated | 262,546 | 60,116 | 22.9% |

Source: [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.12]. Electronics was 66% of revenue and 83% of segment profit.

- **Revenue model:** Electronics sells semi-additive-process (SAP) IC package substrates into AI GPU/ASIC, server CPU, high-end switch and general-purpose server sockets. Ceramics sells diesel particulate filters, EV battery-safety and power-module ceramics, and graphite for nuclear power. "Others" includes construction and other businesses.
- **What drives the P&L:** substrate *area* shipped (die size × layer count), not unit volumes. Management estimates that from CY2026 to CY2030 AI GPU/ASIC unit volume grows 1.8x but SAP area demand grows 5.4x, and server CPU units 1.3x versus 2.5x area [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.12; doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. Total SAP demand index rises 100 (CY26) → 135 → 170 → 210 → 350 (CY30) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.12].
- **Capacity is the binding constraint, not demand.** Ibiden's domestic high-performance capacity index goes 100 (FY3/27) → 150 (FY3/28) → 200 (FY3/30), i.e. 2x, against 3.5–5x market area growth [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.12; doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. Management explicitly says the bottleneck is qualified support engineers, not buildings: even a decision today implies a minimum four years to mass production [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
- **Customer concentration / funding:** the balance sheet shows ¥199.7bn of advances received, up ¥118.8bn in six months [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.5]. This is evidence of customer-backed capacity commitments and reduces stranded-asset risk, but it is not proof of permanent pricing power and it flatters reported operating cash flow.
- **Competitive position:** management describes AI GPU/ASIC substrates moving from a two-supplier structure (Ibiden plus one Taiwanese supplier) to three with a Korean entrant, while insisting aggregate competitor capacity still falls far short of demand [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. Citi reads the same disclosure as a market-share risk that could trigger a temporary de-rating [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].
- **Cyclicality:** Ceramics is auto/industrial-cycle exposed and is guided to only ¥2.1bn of H2 OP on automotive sluggishness [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. Electronics is currently supply-rationed, which suppresses normal cyclicality but raises the eventual normalisation risk.

---

## 3. Latest results and operating drivers

**Company-confirmed facts (H1 FY3/27, Apr–Sep 2026):**

- Revenue ¥262,546m (+34.3% YoY), operating profit ¥60,116m (+84.6%), ordinary profit ¥61,009m (+88.9%), net profit attributable to owners ¥38,574m (+74.8%). Basic EPS ¥68.63, diluted ¥65.10, both restated for the two 2-for-1 splits [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1].
- Gross profit ¥97,705m on cost of sales ¥164,840m → gross margin 37.2% versus 34.7% in H1 FY3/26. SG&A rose only 6.4% to ¥37,589m, so SG&A fell from 18.1% to 14.3% of revenue [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7]. This is the mechanical source of the operating leverage: incremental revenue carried a very high contribution margin.
- Electronics segment profit ¥50,028m on ¥172,540m revenue (29.0%), versus ¥25,429m on ¥113,547m (22.4%) a year earlier [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.11–12].
- Non-operating items were a small positive (¥893m), helped by ¥1,850m interest income and a ¥675m FX gain, partly offset by ¥1,669m depreciation of inactive assets [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7].
- Extraordinary loss of ¥1,650m, mainly ¥1,606m loss on retirement of non-current assets [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7].
- Effective tax rate 34.5% (¥20,490m on ¥59,358m pre-tax) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7].

**Analyst interpretation:** Q2 alone (H1 less Q1) delivered revenue of ~¥139.3bn and OP of ~¥33.2bn, a 23.8% margin, versus Q1's ~¥123.2bn and ~¥26.9bn. That is a ~39% sequential incremental operating margin on ~¥16bn of extra revenue — consistent with premium-mix substrate revenue filling otherwise fixed capacity. The internal note reaches the same conclusion [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast].

**What did *not* drive the result:** Ceramics and Others together contributed ¥10.0bn of H1 segment profit, roughly flat in mix terms; neither is a valuation driver. There was no acquisition, disposal or accounting-policy change in the period [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.3].

**Guidance change:** FY3/27 guidance was raised, and the FY3/28 operating-profit target was lifted from ¥150bn to ¥165bn with the Electronics margin assumption moving from 29% to 31% [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. The FY3/30 target of ¥1,000bn revenue / ¥300bn OP was left unchanged. The shares fell sharply on the day because the medium-term revision was well below market expectations and no Cell 7/Cell 9 investment was announced [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].

---

## 4. Management guidance and expectations

| Metric (¥bn) | FY3/27 guidance | FY3/28 guidance | FY3/30 target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 565.0 | 650.0 | 1,000 |
| Operating profit | 133.0 | 165.0 | 300 |
| Ordinary profit | 134.5 | n/a | n/a |
| Net profit | 89.0 | n/a | n/a |
| EPS (post-split, ¥) | 157.17 | n/a | n/a |

Sources: [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.3]; [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]; [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].

**Key assumptions embedded in guidance (management's own words):**

1. H2 FY3/27 revenue ¥302.5bn, OP ¥72.9bn (24.1% margin), net profit ¥50.4bn; Electronics margin "approaching nearly 30%"; Ceramics H2 OP ¥2.1bn [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
2. FY3/28 Electronics revenue ¥440bn and OP ¥144bn [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].
3. Guidance deliberately embeds future ASP declines: "it is dangerous to optimistically assume current peak pricing will last forever" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. GS estimates the price-decline drag at ~¥10bn of FY3/28 OP [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].
4. The FY3/30 target excludes the newly announced ¥151bn Cell 6 expansion, excludes any use of spare Cell 8 space, and excludes Cell 7/Cell 9 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].

**Available consensus:** only FY3/28 operating profit, ¥190bn, cited by Citi [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. Revenue, net profit and EPS consensus are not available — a genuine data gap, not evidence of mispricing.

**Conflicts I could not reconcile and am preserving:**

- JPM's internal note states the revised FY3/28 plan is group revenue ¥650.0bn / OP **¥163.0bn**, whereas the call transcript and the GS/Citi summaries say **¥165.0bn** [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. I use ¥165bn, the figure repeated in three places, and flag ¥163bn as an unresolved transcription discrepancy.
- The same note gives Electronics FY3/28 as ¥440.0bn revenue / ¥144.0bn OP, which is a 32.7% margin, while the accompanying text and GS describe the assumption as ~31%. The implied margin and the stated margin do not tie; I use the revenue and profit figures and treat the "31%" as approximate.
- JPM's note also contains internally impossible figures (group FY3/26 revenue shown as ¥665.0bn when the filing says ¥565.0bn; FY3/30 group revenue shown as "¥100.0bn"). These are transcription errors in a private note and I have not used them.

---

## 5. Independent forecast

I adopt the verified model's annual frame but state where my own judgement differs.

| ¥bn | FY3/26A | FY3/27E | FY3/28E | FY3/29E |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | [[416.2]] | [[565.0]] | [[665.0]] | [[800.0]] |
| Operating profit | [[62.0]] | [[133.0]] | [[190.0]] | [[220.0]] |
| OP margin | [[14.9]]% | [[23.5]]% | [[28.6]]% | [[27.5]]% |
| Net profit | [[63.7]] | [[89.0]] | [[122.0]] | [[145.0]] |
| EPS (¥, full share) | [[112.5]] | [[157.2]] | [[215.4]] | [[256.0]] |

**FY3/27 — no edge.** The model's [[565.0]]/[[133.0]]/[[89.0]] is arithmetically H1 actual plus the disclosed H2 guidance split, so it cannot differ from guidance. My independent view is that H2 guidance is mildly conservative: H2 implies a 24.1% margin against Q2's 23.8%, despite a richer CPU/switch mix and continued tight supply. A modest beat of ¥3–6bn on OP is plausible, but it is not a differentiated call and I do not build it into the base case.

**FY3/28 — I am below the model and consensus.** The model's [[190.0]] requires FY3/28 quarterly OP to average ~¥47.5bn versus a Q4 FY3/27 run-rate of [[38.8]]. Reversing the ~¥10bn price-decline buffer takes management's ¥165bn to ~¥175bn; the remaining ~¥15bn must come from volume, mix and Cell 8. Cell 8 is a ¥280bn investment that only begins sequential operation from FY2027 (i.e. FY3/28) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.13], and management confirms the bulk of Cell 6/Cell 8 depreciation lands from FY3/28 onward, with much still in construction in progress during FY3/27 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. My range is **¥175–190bn**, and I would not underwrite more than ~¥182bn. The model's [[190.0]] is at the top of my range, not the middle.

**FY3/28 revenue:** the model's [[665.0]] is above management's ¥650.0bn guidance. That is a deliberate model choice (higher volume/mix), not a company number, and it should be read as such.

**FY3/29:** the model's [[800.0]]/[[220.0]] is an interpolation toward the FY3/30 target and depends on Cell 8 full-year loading plus first Cell 6 contribution. Cell 6 operations begin sequentially from FY2029 with contribution "starting in FY2030" per management [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call], so the model's FY3/29 Cell 6 revenue assumption of ¥25bn is, if anything, early. I treat FY3/29 as directional only.

**Quarterly (FY3/27, model):** Q1 [[123.2]]/[[26.9]]/[[17.9]]; Q2 [[139.3]]/[[33.2]]/[[20.7]]; Q3 [[141.2]]/[[34.0]]/[[23.5]]; Q4 [[161.2]]/[[38.8]]/[[26.9]]. The Q3/Q4 split is an assumption built on FY3/26 seasonality, not company disclosure. The internal note's own Q3/Q4 build (¥149.0bn/¥36.5bn and ¥164.5bn/¥41.4bn) is more front-loaded than the model; the difference is immaterial to the annual total.

---

## 6. Forecast bridges

**Revenue, FY3/26 → FY3/27 (base [[416.2]] → [[565.0]]):** +[[95]] Electronics AI-substrate volume (derived from H1 revenue +34.3% applied to the base plus H2 run-rate), +[[30]] pricing/mix (assumption), +[[15]] Ceramics and other recovery (assumption), +[[8.8]] FX and rounding (residual). The residual is small enough to be genuine rounding/FX, not a hidden driver.

**Operating profit, FY3/26 → FY3/27 (base [[62.0]] → [[133.0]]):** +[[50]] Electronics volume/utilisation (derived: H1 OP ¥60.1bn vs ¥32.6bn prior year, plus H2 guided ¥72.9bn), +[[18]] pricing/mix net (assumption), −[[8]] depreciation/startup (assumption), +[[6]] Ceramics and other (assumption), +[[5]] SG&A/other (residual). The +[[5]] residual is disclosed as a residual, not presented as a driver.

**Operating profit, FY3/27 → FY3/28 (base [[133.0]] → [[190.0]]):** +[[45]] volume/utilisation (incremental revenue ¥100bn at ~45% incremental margin), +[[20]] pricing/mix net of decline, −[[12]] depreciation/startup (D&A ¥81bn → ¥90bn), +[[10]] Cell 8 contribution, −[[6]] SG&A/other (residual).

Two cautions on this bridge, which is where I part company with the model:

1. The ~45% incremental operating margin is applied to *all* ¥100bn of incremental revenue, including Ceramics and Others, which run at 10–12% margins. That overstates the group incremental margin unless the mix shift is explicitly modelled. The internal note makes the same point — the incremental margin is high only because incremental revenue is almost entirely advanced Electronics [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast].
2. The +[[20]] pricing/mix line and the +[[45]] volume line risk double counting: if the volume assumption is derived from a revenue growth rate that already embeds price, adding a separate pricing line inflates the total. The model labels the pricing line "derived" but the underlying evidence (GS's ~¥10bn price-decline estimate) supports only ~¥10bn of reversal, not ¥20bn.

**Net profit, FY3/27 → FY3/28 (base [[89.0]] → [[122.0]]):** +[[57]] operating profit, −[[19]] tax at ~33%, −[[5]] minority/other. The 33% tax rate is consistent with the 34.5% H1 effective rate and is reasonable.

**Net profit, FY3/26 → FY3/27 (base [[63.7]] → [[89.0]]):** +[[71]] operating profit, −[[28]] reversal of an FY3/26 one-off gain (assumption — FY3/26 net profit exceeded operating profit, which is unusual and implies non-operating gains), −[[10]] tax/minority, −[[7.7]] other/rounding. The −[[28]] is the single largest assumption in the model and is not directly evidenced in the documents I reviewed; it is economically sensible but unverified.

---

## 7. Consensus and variant perception

**Where I differ:**

| Metric | Period | Guidance | Consensus | Model | My view |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operating profit | FY3/27 | 133.0 | n/a | [[133.0]] | 133–139 (mild beat possible) |
| Operating profit | FY3/28 | 165.0 | 190.0 | [[190.0]] | 175–190 |
| Revenue | FY3/28 | 650.0 | n/a | [[665.0]] | 650–665 |

**The base case does not currently provide a material forecast edge versus the available consensus for FY3/28 operating profit.** The model's [[190.0]] is identical to the Citi-cited consensus. My own range of ¥175–190bn is, if anything, marginally *below* consensus — a mild negative variant, not a positive one.

**Evidence that would confirm the higher end (¥190bn+):** Q3 FY3/27 OP at or above ~¥36bn with Electronics margin above 30%; Cell 8 equipment installation and qualification on schedule; no material ASP erosion in H2 FY3/27; a Cell 7/Cell 9 announcement with customer-backed terms.

**Evidence that would invalidate it:** Q3 OP below ~¥33bn; Electronics margin falling back toward the high-20s; explicit commentary that Cell 8 slips a quarter or more; a customer reallocating volume to a third supplier.

**Where an edge could instead come from:** not from the earnings level, but from (a) the timing of the Cell 7/Cell 9 decision and any FY3/30 target revision, both promised by end-FY3/27 [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]; (b) the possibility that management's conservative ASP assumption is simply wrong in a supply-rationed market; and (c) the negative side — a share-loss narrative that hits the multiple before it hits earnings.

---

## 8. Cash flow and balance sheet

**Operating cash flow quality is the weakest part of the story.** H1 FY3/27 operating cash flow was ¥193,178m, but ¥118,796m of that was the increase in advances received [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9]. Ex-advances, underlying operating cash flow was ~¥74bn. Working capital was otherwise a drag: receivables +¥9,283m, inventories +¥12,018m, partly offset by payables +¥11,183m.

**Capex and free cash flow:**

| ¥bn | H1 FY3/27 | FY3/27E | FY3/28E |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating cash flow | 193.2 (74.4 ex-advances) | n/a | n/a |
| Capex (PP&E + intangibles) | 48.9 | ~200 (call) / 210 (JPM) | ~350 |
| Depreciation | 35.9 | 81.0 | 90.0 |

Sources: [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9–10]; [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]; [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026].

On a normalized basis (EBITDA less capex less cash tax), FY3/28 free cash flow is approximately **−¥110bn**: EBITDA of ~¥280bn (OP [[190.0]] + D&A ~90) against ~¥350bn of capex and ~¥40bn of cash tax. That is a negative FCF yield of roughly −2.4% on the current market capitalisation. The internal note reaches the same conclusion independently [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast]. This is a capital-efficiency and valuation issue, not a liquidity issue.

**Balance sheet (30 Sep 2026):**

- Cash and deposits ¥420,487m; interest-bearing debt ¥162,036m (current bonds ¥10,000m + bonds ¥35,000m + convertible bonds ¥56,036m + long-term loans ¥61,000m) → **net cash ~¥258bn** [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.4–5].
- Equity ratio 53.5%; total assets ¥1,127,606m, up ¥167,180m in six months, driven by cash (+¥124,805m) and advances received (+¥118,796m) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1, p.4–5].
- Construction in progress ¥126,192m, up ¥14,399m — consistent with management's statement that a large part of Cell 6/Cell 8 spend is not yet depreciating [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.4; doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
- Pension liability is immaterial (¥644m). Lease obligations ¥50m. No covenant or refinancing stress is visible.

**Capital allocation:** progressive dividend with a ~20% payout guideline through FY2030; FY3/27 DPS ¥20 post-split (interim ¥10, raised ¥2.5), implying a ~13% payout on EPS of [[157.2]] and a ~0.25% yield at [[8,045]] [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.17; doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.2]. Dividend support is negligible; total return depends on earnings growth and the multiple.

## 9. Valuation

**Method:** forward P/E on FY3/28 EPS, cross-checked with EV/EBITDA. P/E is appropriate because earnings are positive, growing and the capital structure is simple; EV/EBITDA is the necessary cross-check because P/E alone hides the capital intensity and the depreciation that is about to step up.

**Basis:** FY3/28 EPS of [[215.4]] on the model's 566.3m shares; I also show 570.6m basic and ~595m fully diluted. Price [[8,045]].

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| P/E on FY3/27 EPS [[157.2]] | 51.2x |
| P/E on FY3/28 EPS [[215.4]] | 37.3x |
| P/E on FY3/28 EPS, 570.6m shares | 37.6x |
| P/E on FY3/28 EPS, ~595m fully diluted | 39.2x |
| P/E on FY3/29 EPS [[256.0]] | 31.4x |

| EV | ~¥4,306bn |
| EV/EBITDA FY3/27 (OP [[133.0]] + D&A 81) | ~20.1x |
| EV/EBITDA FY3/28 (OP [[190.0]] + D&A 90) | ~15.4x |

**Fair value:** applying 34–39x to FY3/28 EPS of ~¥205–215 gives **¥7,000–8,400**, midpoint ~¥7,700, i.e. roughly −4% from spot. This is consistent with the model's Base of [[7,539]] (−6%) and sits above the model's stated fair-value band of [[5,501]]–[[7,858]].

**Why my band differs from the model's band:** the model strikes its band on FY3/27 EPS of [[157.2]] at 35–50x, while its Base target of [[7,539]] is 35x FY3/28 EPS of [[215.4]]. That mixes two different earnings periods inside one framework. Over a 3–6 month horizon the market will be discounting FY3/28, so I anchor on FY3/28 EPS. The model's own warning acknowledges this construction.

**Why 34–39x is defensible, and why it is not cheap:** the multiple is supported by structural scarcity, customer-funded capacity and a credible path to ¥300bn of OP by FY3/30 (which would be ~¥350 EPS, or ~23x today's price). It is not supported by cash generation — normalized FCF is negative through FY3/29 on the disclosed capex plan — and it offers little protection against a Cell 8 slip, an ASP reset, or a share-loss narrative. A capital-intensive component manufacturer with negative FCF earning 37–39x forward is priced for delivery, not for optionality.

**Sensitivity:** each ¥10bn of FY3/28 OP is worth ~¥12 of EPS (~5.6% of [[215.4]]) and ~¥450/share at 37x. A 5-point multiple change is worth ~¥1,050/share. The multiple, not the earnings, is the dominant near-term swing factor.

## 10. Catalysts within the decision horizon

1. **Q3 FY3/27 results (late January / early February 2027).** The first read on whether H2 guidance of ¥72.9bn OP is conservative. Watch Electronics margin versus 30% and Q3 OP versus ~¥34–36bn.
2. **Cell 7 / Cell 9 investment decision and disclosure, promised by end-FY3/27** [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. Citi names this as the next catalyst. Scale is indicated as similar to Cell 6/Cell 8, i.e. ¥150–280bn each, with customer-backed terms.
3. **Possible revision of the FY3/30 target (¥1,000bn revenue / ¥300bn OP)** alongside that decision. Management has explicitly linked the two [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. This is the single most plausible source of a positive re-rating within the horizon.
4. **EMIB-T mass-production evidence.** Management says the H2-next-year schedule is unchanged and yields are on track, while conceding it is "struggling significantly with yield improvement" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. Any credible yield disclosure is a swing factor.
5. **FY3/27 full-year results (late April 2027)** — at the very edge of the horizon.

**Not catalysts within the horizon:** Cell 6 revenue (operations from FY2029, contribution FY2030), Cell 7/Cell 9 mass production (management says minimum four years from decision), and the FY3/30 target itself. These are real optionality but not 3–6 month events.

---

## 11. Risks and invalidation conditions

- **Business risk — third supplier.** AI GPU/ASIC substrates are moving from two suppliers to three [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call]. Management argues aggregate capacity still falls short of demand; Citi argues the resulting share decline "poses a risk of a temporary stock price correction" [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026]. The multiple, not the earnings, absorbs this first.
- **Forecast risk — Cell 8 timing.** FY3/28 growth depends on sequential Cell 8 output. A delay hits revenue and depreciation absorption simultaneously. Management confirms most Cell 8 depreciation lands from FY3/28 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call].
- **Forecast risk — pricing.** My base case assumes management's embedded ASP declines do not fully occur. If they do, FY3/28 OP is ~¥165bn, not ¥190bn, and EPS falls to ~¥185 — roughly 20% below the model.
- **Cash-flow / balance-sheet risk — capital intensity.** Capex of ~¥200bn (FY3/27), ~¥350bn (FY3/28) and >¥400bn (FY3/29 onward) against negative normalized FCF. Net cash of ~¥258bn is comfortable but not unlimited if Cell 7 and Cell 9 are both approved. Customer advances (¥199.7bn) fund part of this but are a liability, not equity.
- **Dilution risk.** ¥56.0bn of convertible bonds remain at a ¥2,243.1 conversion price; further conversion adds ~25m shares (~4.4% of the base).
- **Valuation risk.** 37–39x FY3/28 EPS and ~15x EV/EBITDA with negative FCF leaves limited cushion. The model's Bear case of [[5,562]] (−31%) is a real, not theoretical, downside if the scarcity premium compresses.
- **Regulatory / geopolitical.** Not a first-order risk in the documents reviewed; the exposure is indirect (customer demand for AI accelerators, Japan-based capacity, Malaysia expansion).
- **Thesis invalidation:** Q3 FY3/27 OP below ~¥33bn, or Electronics margin below ~28%, or explicit confirmation that Cell 8 slips beyond FY3/28, or a customer publicly reallocating AI-GPU volume to a third supplier.

## 13. Key monitoring indicators

1. **Electronics segment operating margin** — 29.0% in H1 FY3/27; management targets "approaching 30%" for H2 and ~35% by FY3/30. A move below 28% would be the first sign of pricing or yield stress.

Cell 6 contribution starts much later, and Cell 8 is currently a depreciation/startup drag rather than a near-term gift.

The market is pricing 4062.T for sustained AI-substrate scarcity, successful Cell 8 ramp, and delivery toward the FY3/30 ¥1,000bn revenue / ¥300bn OP target. - **Model audit incorporated:** The FY3/28 OP bridge adds volume/utilisation and pricing/mix separately while residual SG&A lines are residuals, not independent drivers; [[190.0]] is an assumption stack. The FY3/26 net profit [[63.7]] exceeded OP [[62.0]], and the bridge uses a [[−28]] one-off reversal that is an assumption, not a disclosure. Share count in the model is also modestly flattering because it uses 566.3m versus filing-implied basic ~570.6m and fully diluted ~595m.

FY3/28 normalized FCF is approximately negative ¥110bn on capex of about ¥350bn.
